title: First T2 Year-End Options Generator | Every Date Available
content:
First Year

First T2 Year-End Options Generator

Enter the incorporation date and every month-end available as a first year-end appears, with the length of the year and the T2 date.

Every option, not one testAll within 371 daysT2 date for eachMonth-ends, and why

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

Your incorporation date

Enter the incorporation date and the options appear here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The First Year-End Is a Choice, and It Is Made Once

A corporation picks its own fiscal year-end. Nothing assigns one, and there is no default to fall back on. The choice is made by the first return filed, and from then on the date is fixed on the record.

Changing it afterwards needs the written approval of the Canada Revenue Agency, which makes this the one decision in a corporation’s tax life that is easy now and awkward later. The year-end change impact calculator shows what changing it costs.

The 53-Week Limit Sets the Ceiling

A first tax year may not exceed 53 weeks, which is 371 days counting the day of incorporation. That is what bounds the table: every row in it is within the limit and there is no row beyond it, because a year-end past that point is not available.

The 53-week first tax year checker tests one proposed date against the limit. This page does the opposite and lists them all, which is the more useful order to see them in when the date has not been picked yet.

Why the Table Lists Month-Ends

A year-end does not have to be the last day of a month. Any date inside the limit is available, and a corporation incorporated on the 9th can keep the 9th if it wants to.

Nearly none do, for a reason worth knowing: the six-month filing rule lands on a month-end when the year-end is a month-end, and on an awkward mid-month date when it is not. A month-end year-end makes every date that follows from it easier to hold in your head.

A Later Year-End Is Not a Longer Reprieve

The last row in the table has the longest first year and the latest T2 date, which makes it look like the one that buys the most time. Over one year it does. Over the corporation’s life it buys nothing, because the year-end then recurs annually on that date.

What a later first year-end does buy is one fewer return. A first year ending after two months is a return for two months of nothing, and it is $300.00 plus HST per tax year like any other. Each tax year is its own return whatever its length.

Where the first year-end fallsFirst tax yearReturns in the first two yearsWhat it costs you
The earliest month-end availableA few weeksTwoA return for a few weeks of nothing
A month-end around twelve months outClose to a full yearOneThe usual choice
The latest month-end inside 53 weeksUp to 371 daysOneThe latest first deadline, and that date every year after

Frequently Asked Questions

How long can my first tax year be?

Up to 53 weeks, which is 371 days counting the day of incorporation. Every date the generator lists is inside that limit.

Does a year-end have to be the end of a month?

No. Any date within the 53-week limit is available. Month-ends are what nearly every corporation chooses, because the six-month filing rule then lands on a month-end too.

Can I change the year-end later?

Only with the written approval of the Canada Revenue Agency. The date is fixed by the first return filed, and a later return carrying a different date is rejected rather than treated as a change.

Is a short first year cheaper?

No. A short first year is a separate return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, so choosing a very early first year-end means paying for a return covering a few weeks of nothing.

Which option should I pick?

That depends on facts a web page does not have. What the generator can tell you is which dates are available and what each one does to the filing deadline.

title: Year-End Change Impact Calculator | The Period It Creates
content:
Date Tool

Year-End Change Impact Calculator

Moving a fiscal year-end creates a period and a return. Enter both dates for its length, its T2 date and what comes after it.

Shows the period createdTests the 371-day limitGives both T2 datesWritten CRA approval required

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The two year-ends

Enter both year-ends and the effect appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Change of Year-End Creates a Period, and a Return

Moving a year-end does not stretch or shrink the year that is already running. It closes a period on the new date, and that period is a tax year of its own with its own return and its own deadline.

So a change from December 31 to June 30 produces a six-month period, a return for it, and then full years ending June 30. The cost of the change is that extra return, at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

How a year-end movesWhat creates the periodApproval needed
An approved changeThe new date closes a period earlyWritten approval from the Canada Revenue Agency
An amalgamationEach predecessor’s year ends the day beforeNone, the amalgamation sets it
A dissolutionThe final period ends on the dissolution dateNone, the dissolution sets it

The Approval Is the Part That Is Not Automatic

A fiscal year-end is fixed by the first return filed. Changing it needs the written approval of the Canada Revenue Agency, and the request is made before the change rather than demonstrated by filing.

A return filed carrying a year-end that does not match the record is not read as a change of year-end. It is rejected against the date on record, which means the year is still outstanding and the transmission achieved nothing. The corporate fiscal year end calculator works from the date on record.

The New Date Cannot Be More Than 53 Weeks Out

A tax year cannot exceed 53 weeks, which is 371 days. Where the gap between the current year-end and the proposed one is longer than that, the gap is not a single period and cannot be reported as one.

Reaching a year-end that far out means an intervening year-end first, so two returns rather than one. The calculator says so where the dates you enter have that effect.

A Short Period Does Not Get an Early Deadline

The six-month rule runs from the day the period ends, whatever the period’s length. A two-month stub has six months after it to file, which is three times the period itself.

What a short period does bring forward is the next year-end, and with it the next return. The two T2 returns in one year checker shows how close together two deadlines can land after a change like this.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I change my corporation’s fiscal year-end?

With the written approval of the Canada Revenue Agency. The request is made before the change, and filing a return with a different date on it does not change the year-end on record.

Does changing a year-end mean an extra return?

Usually yes. The change closes a period on the new date and that period is a tax year with its own return, at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

How long can the period created be?

No longer than 53 weeks, which is 371 days. A gap longer than that is not one tax year and needs an intervening year-end.

When is the return for that period due?

Six months after the day the period ends, moved to the next business day where that falls on a weekend or a public holiday. A short period gets the same six months as a full year.

What happens if I just file on the new date?

The return is rejected against the year-end on record. The year stays outstanding, so nothing has been filed and nothing has been changed.

title: Two T2 Returns in One Year Checker | Both Deadlines
content:
Date Tool

Two T2 Returns in One Year Checker

Two tax years can both come due in one calendar year. Enter the two year-ends for both deadlines, the gap and the total.

Both T2 datesDays between themFlags a tight gapEach year is its own return

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The two year-ends

Enter both year-ends and both deadlines appear here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Three Ways a Corporation Ends Up With Two

A short first year followed by a full one is the commonest. A corporation incorporated in October with a December 31 year-end has a three-month first year and then a full one, and both returns come due within six months of each other.

An approved change of year-end is the second, and a final period ending at dissolution is the third. In each case the two periods are separate tax years, and nothing about them being close together merges them.

How it happensThe two periodsReturns owed
Incorporated part-way through a yearA short first tax year, then a full oneOne for each
An approved change of year-endA stub period at the changeover, then full yearsOne for each
Dissolved part-way through a yearA full year, then a short final periodOne for each

Two Deadlines Close Together Read as One

This is the practical failure. Two dates a few months apart look like one obligation, the later one gets filed, and the earlier year sits outstanding without anyone noticing, often for years.

An unfiled year does not expire. It stays open, invites a demand to file, and blocks a clearance certificate. The unfiled years checker is the page for working out whether this has already happened.

Two Returns Means Two Returns

Each tax year is its own return whatever its length, so two periods in one calendar year are two returns at $300.00 plus HST per tax year each. A three-month period is not a part-return and is not priced as one.

They can be prepared and transmitted together, which is how a catch-up is handled, and they are prepared oldest first because the closing balances of the first year open the second.

Why the Order Cannot Be Reversed

The second return opens from figures the first one establishes: retained earnings, the undepreciated balance on Schedule 8, the loss continuity. Filing the later year first means filing opening figures that have not been reported yet.

The retained earnings rollforward calculator gives the figure the second year has to open from.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a corporation file two T2 returns in one year?

Yes, and it must where two tax years end close together. A short first year followed by a full one, an approved change of year-end and a final period at dissolution all produce two.

Do two returns cost twice as much?

Yes. Each tax year is its own return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year whatever the length of the period it covers.

Can both be filed at the same time?

They can be prepared and transmitted together. They are prepared oldest first, because the closing balances of the earlier year open the later one.

What if I only filed the later one?

The earlier year is outstanding. It does not expire, it invites a demand to file, and it blocks a clearance certificate until it is filed.

Is the deadline for the short period earlier?

No. The six-month rule runs from the day each period ends, so a short period gets the same six months as a full year.

title: Mandatory T2 E-Filing Checker | Tax Years After 2023
content:
Filing Method

Mandatory T2 E-Filing Checker

Electronic filing is mandatory for tax years starting after 2023. Enter the first day of the tax year to see which side it falls on.

One date decides itTax years starting after 2023Matters most on a catch-upEvery return here is electronic

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The tax year

Enter the first day of the tax year.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Rule Turns on One Date

Electronic filing of the T2 is mandatory for tax years starting after 2023. There is no revenue test and no size test in it: a tax year beginning on or after January 1, 2024 is inside the rule and one beginning earlier is not.

Note that the date tested is the first day of the tax year, not the year-end and not the day the return is filed. A year that began in December 2023 and ended in November 2024 began before the rule.

Tax year beginsElectronic filingWhat it means on a catch-up
Before January 1, 2024Not mandatoryPaper was an option for these years
On or after January 1, 2024MandatoryFiling on paper carries a penalty

Where This Actually Matters: a Catch-Up

For a single current year the answer is academic, because the return is going to be transmitted electronically either way. It matters on a catch-up, where the oldest years in the sequence may predate the rule while the newest sit inside it.

That is a sequence filed under two regimes at once, which is worth knowing about and makes no difference to how it is done. The catch-up filing schedule generator lays out the years and their dates.

Filing on Paper Where It Is Mandatory Carries a Penalty

There is a penalty for filing on paper where electronic filing is required. This page does not state the amount, and that is deliberate: a penalty figure read off a web page is a figure read from the wrong place.

The guide to mandatory T2 electronic filing is where that sits. What this checker answers is the prior question, which is whether the requirement reaches the year in front of you.

Every Return Filed Here Is Transmitted Electronically

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada, and that is true of years the rule never reached as much as years inside it.

So the practical answer for a visitor is that this changes nothing about their filing. You sign Form T183CORP and the return is transmitted. The Form T183CORP signature requirement checker covers that step.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is electronic T2 filing mandatory?

For tax years starting after 2023, yes. A tax year beginning on or after January 1, 2024 is inside the requirement.

Which date does the rule test?

The first day of the tax year, not the year-end and not the filing date. A year that began in December 2023 began before the rule.

Is there a revenue threshold?

Not in this rule. It turns on when the tax year started, which is why one date answers it.

What happens if a return is filed on paper?

There is a penalty for filing on paper where electronic filing is required. The amount is not stated here; the guide to mandatory T2 electronic filing covers it.

Does this change how my nil return is filed?

No. Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer and transmits every return electronically, including years the requirement never reached.

title: Business Days Between Dates Calculator | Ontario Holidays
content:
Date Tool

Business Days Between Dates Calculator

Enter two dates for the calendar days, the business days, the weekend days and every Ontario public holiday in the span.

Counts both endsNine Ontario holidaysNames each holidayThe calendar every date tool here uses

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The two dates

Enter both dates and the counts appear here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Calendar Days and Business Days Answer Different Questions

A deadline runs on calendar days. The work of meeting it runs on business days, and on a short span the two differ by enough to change a decision: ten calendar days over a long weekend is six business days.

A demand to file is where this bites hardest, because the letter names a date that may be close. The CRA demand to file deadline calculator does both counts against a letter.

The Nine Holidays, and Whose They Are

The calendar here is Ontario’s nine public holidays under the Employment Standards Act: New Year’s Day, Family Day, Good Friday, Victoria Day, Canada Day, Labour Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day and Boxing Day.

Good Friday moves every year because it is derived from Easter, and Family Day, Victoria Day, Labour Day and Thanksgiving Day are each defined by a weekday rather than a date. The calculator works all of them out rather than reading them from a table, so no year is missing.

Public holidayHow the date is set
New Year’s DayJanuary 1
Family DayThe third Monday in February
Good FridayTwo days before Easter Sunday, so it moves each year
Victoria DayThe Monday on or before May 24
Canada DayJuly 1
Labour DayThe first Monday in September
Thanksgiving DayThe second Monday in October
Christmas DayDecember 25
Boxing DayDecember 26

Every Date Tool Here Runs on This Calendar

This matters more than it sounds. A site with forty date tools can easily end up with two holiday lists and two answers for the same date, and a visitor who notices has no way to tell which one to trust.

There is one list, in one shared module, and every tool calls it. The due date weekend and holiday shift calculator shows the shift a single date gets from it.

A Holiday on a Weekend Is Counted Once

Where a public holiday falls on a Saturday or a Sunday, this counts it as a weekend day and not again as a holiday. That keeps the three counts adding up to the calendar total, which is the property that makes them checkable.

It also means such a holiday does not appear in the list of named holidays below the counts. The list is the holidays that cost a business day, not every holiday in the span.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many business days are between two dates?

Enter both and the calculator counts them. Both dates are included, so a Monday to the following Monday is eight calendar days.

Which holidays does this use?

Ontario’s nine public holidays under the Employment Standards Act. It is the same calendar every date tool on this site runs on.

Are both dates counted?

Yes. The span is inclusive at both ends, which is how a filing period is normally read.

What about a holiday that falls on a weekend?

It is counted once, as a weekend day, so the three counts still add up to the calendar total. It is not listed among the named holidays.

Does this apply outside Ontario?

The holiday list is Ontario’s. A province with a different list will differ on a span containing one of its own holidays.

title: Form T183CORP Signature Requirement Checker | Who Signs
content:
T183CORP

Form T183CORP Signature Requirement Checker

Form T183CORP needs an authorized signing officer, signed before transmission. Three answers show whether those conditions are met.

Authorized signing officerSigned before transmissionDate and HH:MM:SS, EasternKept six years, not sent to CRA

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The signature

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What Form T183CORP Is For

Form T183CORP is the authorization that lets a return be transmitted electronically on a corporation’s behalf. It carries the figures on your own return, and signing it is how you confirm those figures before anything is sent.

It is always Form T183CORP. The name is never shortened on this site, because the shorter name belongs to a different authorization for a different return and the two are not interchangeable.

An Authorized Signing Officer, Not Just Anyone Involved

The form is signed by an authorized signing officer of the corporation. A bookkeeper, a spouse, a shareholder who is not an officer and the accountant preparing the return are none of them that, however closely they are involved.

The officer also has to have read the figures. The signature is a confirmation of the return’s contents, so signing without reading it is not the thing the form is asking for.

Who it isCan sign Form T183CORP
An authorized signing officer of the corporationYes
A shareholder who is not an officerNo
The bookkeeperNo
The accountant who prepared the returnNo
A spouse or family member who is not an officerNo

Before Transmission, and the Timestamp Proves It

The form is signed before the return is transmitted, not alongside it and not afterwards. It authorizes the transmission, so it has to exist first.

Here it is signed on a single-use access-controlled screen, and the date and the hour, minute and second are recorded on the server in Eastern Time. It is never backdated. The timestamp is written as you sign, which is what makes the sequence demonstrable rather than asserted.

The Firm Keeps It for Six Years and Does Not Send It

The signed form stays with Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation for six years. It is not sent to the Canada Revenue Agency unless the Canada Revenue Agency asks for it.

That surprises people who expect the signature to travel with the return. It does not. The transmission carries the return; the form is the record of the signature that permitted it, held in case it is ever asked for. The guide to T183CORP signing and transmission sets out the whole sequence.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can sign Form T183CORP?

An authorized signing officer of the corporation. A bookkeeper, a non-officer shareholder or the accountant preparing the return cannot sign it in that officer’s place.

When is Form T183CORP signed?

Before the return is transmitted. It authorizes the transmission, so it has to exist first, and the timestamp recorded as you sign shows that it did.

Is Form T183CORP sent to CRA?

No, unless the Canada Revenue Agency asks for it. The transmission carries the return; the signed form is the record of the signature that permitted it.

How long is it kept?

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation keeps the signed form for six years.

Can the form be backdated?

No. The date and the hour, minute and second are written by the server in Eastern Time as you sign.

title: Provincial Return Requirement Checker | CO-17 and AT1
content:
Provincial

Provincial Return Requirement Checker

Quebec and Alberta each collect their own corporate tax. Two answers show whether CO-17 or AT1 is a separate return to file.

Quebec: CO-17Alberta: AT1Separate returns, separate filingsNot covered by the fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

Where the corporation operates

Answer both questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Two Provinces Collect Their Own Corporate Tax

In most of Canada the province levies its corporate income tax through the federal return, so one T2 settles both. Quebec and Alberta do not. Each administers its own corporate tax and each has its own return.

Quebec’s is CO-17, filed with Revenu Quebec. Alberta’s is AT1. Both are separate returns in their own right, not schedules attached to the T2 and not something the T2 covers.

Where the corporation operatesCorporate income tax returnsCovered by the fee
QuebecThe federal T2 and CO-17The T2 only
AlbertaThe federal T2 and AT1The T2 only
Everywhere elseThe federal T2 on its ownThe T2

A Quiet Year Is Quiet on Both Returns

A corporation with no activity has nothing to report provincially either, so the provincial return for that year is nil in the same way the federal one is.

Being nil does not make it optional. It is a separate return, filed separately, on its own deadline, and the obligation follows from the permanent establishment rather than from there being anything to report.

What the Fee Covers, Said Plainly

The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers one nil federal T2 return for one corporation for one tax year. CO-17 is not covered by it, and neither is AT1.

That is worth being direct about rather than leaving a visitor to discover it. The nil T2 filing cost page sets out the whole boundary of what sits inside the fee and what does not.

The Registry Annual Return Is a Different Thing

Every corporation also owes an annual return to the registry it is incorporated with, federally or provincially. That is a registry filing confirming the directors and the registered office, and it reports no income.

It is easy to hear "provincial return" and think of that one. They are unrelated obligations with different consequences: missing a registry annual return gets a corporation struck, which the involuntary dissolution risk checker covers.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Quebec have a separate corporate tax return?

Yes. CO-17 is a separate provincial return, filed with Revenu Quebec. It is not part of the federal T2.

Does Alberta have one?

Yes. AT1 is a separate provincial return in the same way.

Is CO-17 or AT1 covered by the fee?

No. The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers one nil federal T2 return for one corporation for one tax year.

What about the other provinces?

Elsewhere the province levies its corporate income tax through the federal return, so the T2 is the only corporate income tax return.

Is a nil provincial return still required?

The obligation follows the permanent establishment rather than there being something to report, so a nil year is still a return to file.

title: CRA Account Closure Sequencer | What Order and What It Costs
content:
Accounts

CRA Account Closure Sequencer

Payroll and GST/HST accounts outlive the activity that opened them. Three answers give the order of closure and what each step costs.

Ordered stepsForm RC145 closes two of themSays what is outside the feeReturns come first

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

What is open

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Accounts Outlive the Activity That Opened Them

A business number carries separate accounts: corporate income tax, payroll, GST/HST. Each is opened for a reason and each stays open until it is closed, whatever happens to the reason.

That is how a dormant corporation ends up with obligations it has no activity to match. The payroll account from when it had staff and the GST/HST account from when it was registered both keep generating returns and remittances, separately from the T2.

Account on the business numberWhat it is forHow it closesCovered by the fee
Corporate income taxThe T2 returnIt ends with the corporationThe nil return is
PayrollT4 returns and remittances, including nil onesForm RC145No
GST/HSTGST/HST returns, including nil onesForm RC145No

The Outstanding Returns Come First

Closing an account does not clear what was owed on it, and it does not file anything. A closure on top of unfiled years leaves the unfiled years exactly where they were.

So the sequence starts with the returns. The unfiled years checker identifies which are outstanding and the catch-up filing schedule generator dates them.

Form RC145 Closes Both of the Accounts That Matter Here

One form closes a payroll account and the same form closes a GST/HST account. Until an account is closed, nil returns and nil remittances remain due on it.

Neither closure is covered by the nil T2 fee, which is one of the clearest boundaries on the site: the fee is for a return, and closing an account is not a return. The GST/HST account closure checker and the payroll nil remittance checker each go further into one of them.

Why the Order Is Not Arbitrary at a Wind-Up

A clearance request rests on a complete filing record, so it comes after the returns rather than alongside them. The registry filing comes last, because dissolving a corporation that still owes returns leaves the tax years open behind it.

Out of order, each step still happens but none of them finishes the job. The dissolution readiness checker tests whether the corporation is ready for the last step.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I close a CRA payroll or GST/HST account?

With Form RC145, which closes either one. Until the account is closed, nil returns and nil remittances remain due on it.

Should I close the accounts before filing the returns?

No. Closing an account does not file anything and does not clear what was owed on it, so the outstanding returns come first.

Is closing an account covered by the fee?

No. The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year is for a nil T2 return. An account closure is not a return and sits outside it.

Why does a dormant corporation still owe anything?

Because the obligation follows the open account rather than the activity. An account nobody closed keeps generating returns and remittances.

Where does the clearance certificate come in the order?

After the returns, including the final one, because the request rests on a complete filing record. The registry dissolution comes after that.

content:
Calendar

Corporate Deadline Calendar Generator

One year-end in, the whole corporate calendar out: the balance date, the T2 date, the T4 date, the annual return and the next year-end.

One input, every dateAll on one holiday calendarShows what is outside the feeLinks each date to its own tool

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

Your corporation

Enter the year-end and answer both questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Every Date a Corporation Owes, From One Year-End

The single-purpose tools on this site each answer one date well. What they do not do is show you the shape of a year, which is what someone who has just picked a year-end actually wants.

This page restates dates those tools own and links to each of them. Where you want one date in depth, follow the link; where you want to see how they sit together, stay here.

Not Every Date Derives From the Year-End

Two of the rows do not. The T4 information return reports a calendar year and is due at the end of the following February whatever year-end the corporation uses, so a June year-end puts the T2 in December and the T4 at the end of February.

The federal annual return runs from the incorporation anniversary, which is why this page asks for that date separately. The federal annual return anniversary calculator is the page for that one on its own.

ObligationMeasured fromCovered by the fee
Balance of taxTwo months after the fiscal year-end, or three for a qualifying CCPCNothing is owed on a nil year
The T2 returnSix months after the fiscal year-endYes
The T4 information returnThe calendar year, due at the end of the following FebruaryNo
The federal annual return60 days after the incorporation anniversaryNo

Which of These the Fee Covers

One of them. The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the nil T2 return. The registry annual return is a registry filing and sits outside it, and so does the T4 information return and any account closure.

Saying that on the calendar rather than in the small print is the point of the third column. A visitor should be able to see the whole obligation and the boundary of the service in the same table.

Every Row Moves Off a Weekend the Same Way

Each date here is moved to the next business day where it falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or an Ontario public holiday, on the one shared holiday calendar. Two rows can shift by different amounts, which is correct rather than inconsistent.

The balance row assumes the two-month period. A Canadian-controlled private corporation meeting the conditions has three months, which the corporate balance due date calculator handles.

Frequently Asked Questions

What deadlines does a corporation have each year?

A balance of tax date two months after the year-end, or three for a qualifying CCPC, the T2 six months after it, the registry annual return, and a T4 information return where a payroll account is open.

Which of them does a nil corporation actually have to meet?

The T2 filing date and the registry annual return. A nil year has no balance to pay, so the earlier date passes with nothing owed on it.

Why does the T4 date not follow my year-end?

Because the T4 reports a calendar year. It is due at the end of the following February whatever fiscal year-end the corporation uses.

Why do you need my incorporation date?

The federal annual return runs from the incorporation anniversary, not from the fiscal year-end, so that row cannot be derived from the year-end.

Are all these dates covered by the fee?

No. The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the nil T2 return. The registry annual return, the T4 return and account closures all sit outside it.

The outstanding years

Enter the earliest unfiled year-end and the number of years.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

This Is the Third of Three Catch-Up Tools

The family has two already and they answer different questions, so it is worth saying which is which rather than leaving you to find out.

The unfiled years checker works out which years are outstanding. The unfiled years cost calculator gives what the whole catch-up costs. This page gives the dated schedule: a row per year, with its deadline and how overdue it is.

What you want to knowThe tool that answers it
Which years are outstandingUnfiled years checker
What the whole catch-up costsUnfiled years cost calculator
The dated schedule, a row per yearThis page

Oldest First Is Not a Preference

Each year’s return opens from the closing balances of the one before it: retained earnings, the undepreciated balance on Schedule 8, the loss continuity. A year filed out of order carries opening figures that have not been established.

That is why the schedule is numbered. The order is part of the work rather than a tidy way of presenting it, and the retained earnings rollforward calculator is what carries one year’s closing figure into the next.

Prepared in Order, Transmitted Together

The years are prepared in sequence and can then be transmitted in one sitting. You sign one Form T183CORP for each year, because each year is its own return and each transmission needs its own signature.

Each year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year, so the total is the number of years at that price. There is no discount for volume and no part-year rate: a three-month stub period is a return like any other.

What the Overdue Column Does and Does Not Say

It counts days past the filing deadline, which is a fact about the calendar. It is not a penalty calculation and it does not grow into one on a true nil year.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

The nil return late penalty checker works through that distinction properly, and the guide to catching up on unfiled corporate tax returns sets out the whole process.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I catch up on several unfiled T2 returns?

Oldest first, because each year opens from the closing balances of the one before it. Once prepared they can be transmitted together.

How much does a catch-up cost?

Each tax year is its own return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, so the total is the number of outstanding years at that price.

Can several years be filed at once?

They are prepared in order and can then be transmitted in one sitting. You sign one Form T183CORP for each year.

Does an unfiled year eventually expire?

No. It stays open, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, and blocks a clearance certificate until it is filed.

Does the overdue count mean I owe a penalty?

It counts days past the deadline, not money. On a true nil year the percentage late-filing penalty is a percentage of tax owing, and the corporation owes $0.00.
